options.title: Raise s_valid with start in the frame source
options.approach: In frame_src, precompute word 0 from the configuration, which is quasi-static, so s_valid and s_data are asserted in the same clock as `start`. This removes the fs_start register stage. The checksum logic, the receive side and the crossing are not changed.

gain.basis_note: fs_start adds 1 clock and the stage file allows at most 1 to be removed, so the gain is 0 to 1 clock. The low end is 0 because the MAC may still need s_valid a clock later.
gain.ceiling_basis: the removable clocks of the touched stages, per the stage file (1)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: Small RTL change. The worst setup path (0.115 ns) ends in frame_src, so a timing re-route may be needed.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run

options.title: Shorten the go-pulse crossing by one clock
options.approach: In core, shorten the xpm_cdc_pulse u_p_go crossing by one clock, for example by removing the output register or using a leaner pulse crossing. Keep the 2 synchroniser flops where the failure rate allows it. The order bus and its 3-flop crossing are not changed; check that frame_src still finds the bus settled when the earlier pulse arrives.

gain.basis_note: cross_go adds 4 clocks, of which the stage file allows 1 to be removed. The low end is 0 if the order bus is not yet settled and the change has to be dropped.
gain.ceiling_basis: the removable clocks of the touched stages, per the stage file (1)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: The change is small, but it needs a CDC report and a board run to confirm it.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run

risk.summary: A shorter crossing lowers the metastability margin, and the bus may not be settled when the earlier pulse arrives. Simulation cannot show either effect.
risk.contract_note: The change stays inside core. Only the pulse timing seen by frame_src moves, and it is checked against the bus-settling rule.

options.title: Transmit-side chain: start, preamble and the frame source
options.approach: Take the O1 change (word 0 precomputed, s_valid with start) and also merge the mac64_tx output register (mac_preamble) so the preamble word goes into pcs_tx without its own register. The preamble does not depend on the frame data. The gearbox pause rule and the CRC logic behind the register are kept, and the receive side and the crossing are not changed.

gain.basis_note: fs_start and mac_preamble add 1 clock each, and the stage file allows 1 clock out of each, so at most 2. The low end is 0 because mac_preamble has only 1.132 ns slack and tx_encode only 1.103 ns, so merging may not close timing.
gain.ceiling_basis: the removable clocks of the touched stages, per the stage file (2)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: The logic added in front of the encode register may take several timing rounds, and the pause behaviour needs more benches.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run

options.title: All removable stages on the receive-to-transmit chain
options.approach: Apply the O1 and O2 changes and the O3 merge of mac_preamble. Also merge the pcs_rx descramble and decode (rx_descramble) into the block-extraction register, and fold the trade64 decision register (decide) forward. The tx_encode and tx_spill stages are not changed, nor are the GT and its 64-bit interface (gt_wizard stays as it is).

gain.basis_note: Each of the five touched stages has removable = 1 clock in the stage file, so at most 5 of the 11 chain clocks. The low end of 1 allows for several merges not closing timing. rx_mac is not touched, so the maximum from stage file is 5.
gain.ceiling_basis: the removable clocks of the touched stages, per the stage file (5)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: Five separate changes, each needing timing closure, with a board run for the crossing. The recorded build takes about 1177 s per run.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run
